about.label: Paper spacecraft
about.text: Engines and ships that were designed in detail and never built, each from its own study: Discovery II, NASA's DRA 5.0 nuclear thermal Mars ship, NASA's HOPE ships to Callisto, Project Longshot, the Orion nuclear pulse ship, the fission fragment rocket, gaseous core engines and the Starshot sail. They fly on SSE4's own physics, marked not yet built.
about.note: Track RK, package RK6 (handover/design/SSE4-atomic-rockets-plan.md section 6). Published on Explorers, not built into SSE4. Built by scripts/build-paper-spacecraft.py; do not edit by hand.

credit: Figures from NASA, NASA contractor and US Naval Academy reports (US Government works) and from Parkin 2018 (arXiv:1805.01306); each figure names its study. Our selection, arrangement and words are Apache-2.0.

paper.longshot-icf.name: Longshot inertial fusion pulse drive (D-He3 pellets)

paper.discovery-ii-jupiter.derived: thrust 6,250 lbf in newtons; exhaust from 35,435 s; the two settings are one 4,830 MW jet geared for Jupiter and Saturn; jet efficiency 0.8 is the study's assumption; mass_t is the fusion reactor line of Table 1

paper.discovery-ii-saturn.derived: thrust 4,690 lbf in newtons; exhaust from 47,205 s

paper.hope-mtf.derived: thrust = 2 x jet power (2.071 GW) / exhaust (77,000 s): the paper gives no newtons; efficiency = jet over jet plus the 176.5 MW and 33.9 MW its radiators shed

paper.hope-mpd.derived: thrust = 2 x 24 MW / exhaust (8,000 s); efficiency = 24 MW of jet over 37 MW in

paper.longshot-icf.derived: exhaust from 1.02e6 s; thrust 1,838 N read from the OCR of the tank-sizing appendix

paper.orion-10m.derived: the reports give no average thrust; this is the 0.3 g start-up of GA-5009 on the 599,000 kg departure mass of GA-4891; exhaust from 1,800 s, the low end of 1,800 to 2,500 s; module 200,000 lb

paper.pewee-25klbf.derived: thrust 25 klbf in newtons; exhaust from 900 s, the value the DRA 5.0 analysis used (900 s at 2650 K to 910 s at 2700 K; ~906 s in the 2012 paper); engine mass not given (thrust-to-weight about 3.4)

paper.ffre.derived: thrust 10 lbf in newtons; exhaust from 527,000 s; efficiency = jet over 1000 MW thermal (the report says about 11%); 1350 K is its heat-shield radiator, which sheds 699 MW

paper.nuclear-light-bulb.derived: thrust 92,000 lb in newtons; exhaust from 1870 s; efficiency = jet over the 4600 MW engine power; mass 70,000 lb

paper.open-cycle-gas-core.derived: thrust 50,000 lb; exhaust from 5200 s; engine 250,000 lb with its radiator (1100 K from Ragsdale and Willis). As printed its jet (5.7 GW) is more than its 5,000 MW reactor: the books do not close, and the reading says so

nav_ships.about: Ships from design studies, fitted with their engines so the power books set the drive. Each has a recipe saying what the study claimed.

paper.hope-nep.name: HOPE nuclear electric ship to Callisto (piloted)

study_says.note: one way, from and to C3 ~ 0 (no spiral counted)

paper.discovery-ii.derived: dry_t is IMLEO less the main-impulse hydrogen (807 mt) and the D-He3 (11 mt); reaction control, reserve and residuals stay aboard
paper.discovery-ii.about: A 240 m crewed fusion ship designed to make the voyages of the film 2001 real: six crew, 172 t of payload, a 4.8 GW jet.

study_says.note: one way; the same ship geared to a faster exhaust and less thrust

paper.discovery-ii-saturn.derived: as the Jupiter ship; IMLEO 1,690 mt (Table 2 prints 1,699 for Saturn, but the text says the masses were fixed for both)
paper.discovery-ii-saturn.about: The same Discovery II, geared for Saturn: the same jet power spent on a faster, thinner exhaust.

paper.hope-mtf.study: HOPE (Human Outer Planet Exploration), magnetised target fusion

study_says.note: outbound; 183 days at Callisto, about 652 days in all, departing 27 Apr 2045

paper.hope-mtf.derived: dry_t is IML1 less the 142,000 main propellant; the reaction control propellant stays aboard
paper.hope-mtf.about: NASA's 2003 study of a crewed base on Callisto, flown by a fusion drive of 77,000 seconds.

study_says.note: flight time, thrusting about 812 days; about 120 days at Callisto, about 1,661 days in all

paper.hope-nep.derived: dry_t is IML1 less the 577,000 propellant
paper.hope-nep.about: The same Callisto mission on 37 MW of reactor electricity and magnetoplasmadynamic thrusters: the slow, honest way.

study_says.note: about 100 years, turning over at 71.27 years and braking into orbit about Beta Centauri (the report says 4.3 light years, sec. 3.4); cruising near 5% of light speed; no crew

paper.longshot.derived: dry_t is the overall total (396.414 t) less the fuel (264.276 t); the OCR of the weight table is garbled
paper.longshot.about: A 1988 student design for NASA: an uncrewed fusion probe that reaches Alpha Centauri in about a century.

paper.orion-mars.study: Orion nuclear pulse, 10 m module, Mars by orbital rendezvous
paper.orion-mars.derived: dry_t from the rocket equation: 599,000 kg at departure over exp(22.2 km/s / 17.65 km/s); thrust is the 0.3 g start-up
paper.orion-mars.about: Pushed by a bomb a second against a 10 m plate: the 1964 design for a Saturn V-launched Mars ship with eight crew.

paper.dra5-ntr.study: NASA Mars Design Reference Architecture 5.0, nuclear thermal crew vehicle (4-launch, twin drop tanks)

study_says.note: 180 days each way, about 540 at Mars, about 900 in all; ideal delta-v without gravity losses

paper.dra5-ntr.derived: dry_t is the ~333 t IMLEO less the ~180.2 t of usable hydrogen; the real ship drops its two drop tanks after the Earth departure burn, which a single-stage record cannot (it carries their mass to Mars). The arrays are held at their 50 kWe at Mars rather than following the starlight
paper.dra5-ntr.about: Three Rover-descended 25,000 lbf nuclear engines on one stage, six crew, Mars and back in about 900 days: NASA's own reference design.

paper.ffre-callisto.study: Fission fragment rocket engine, crewed Callisto mission

study_says.note: 'over 2100 days were needed to reach the orbit of Jupiter'

paper.ffre-callisto.derived: dry_t is the wet mass less the 4.0 mT of uranium dioxide dust
paper.ffre-callisto.about: Fission fragments thrown straight out at 1.7% of light speed: half a million seconds of impulse, and 10 lbf of thrust.

paper.starshot.waits_on: RK5: a beamed leg that depends on its sender (the travel thread)
paper.starshot.about: A 3.6 g sail thrown to a fifth of light speed by 200 GW of laser in nine minutes.

advances.name: Nuclear light bulb
advances.note: uranium plasma held in a quartz bulb, its light heating hydrogen outside: 1870 s, 92,000 lb, 4600 MW

advances.name: Open-cycle gas core
advances.note: a uranium plasma ball inside flowing hydrogen, some of it lost with the exhaust: 5200 s from 5,000 MW

advances.name: Nuclear pulse (Orion)

least_size.what: fissile metal per pulse unit at most: a bare sphere of 93 to 94% U-235 goes critical at 53.9 kg, so a fission charge needs a share of that and cannot be made arbitrarily small; plutonium and a reflector lower it

advances.note: within the reach of 1960s engineering in General Atomic's view; never built (1963 test ban)

advances.name: Magnetised target fusion drive
advances.note: plant_w_per_kg from 0.0193 kg per kW of jet (derived)

advances.name: Fission fragment rocket
advances.note: waste_per_jet = heat over jet at 1000 MW thermal (derived); most of it leaves at 1350 K

advances.name: Megawatt magnetoplasmadynamic thruster
advances.note: electric: thrust is set by the power plant

advances.name: Space fission reactor with Brayton conversion
advances.note: Prometheus's goal of 50 kg per kWe; two 100 kWe Brayton units designed for the Jupiter Icy Moons Orbiter (mason2003), cancelled 2005

stops.caption: Discovery II puts 4.8 billion watts into its exhaust, a large power station's output, for 28 kN of thrust. On 1,690 tonnes that is less than two thousandths of a g.
stops.try: Open the power line and read the jet power.

stops.caption: Thrust times exhaust speed is twice the jet power. Faster exhaust saves fuel, but at fixed power it gives less push: the same engine geared for Saturn has a quarter less thrust.
stops.try: Switch to the Saturn setting and compare the acceleration.

stops.caption: With reactor electricity instead of fusion, 37 MW buys about a ninth of the HOPE fusion ship's push. The same trip to Callisto takes more than three times as long.
stops.try: Plan the trip and compare the days.

stops.caption: Half a million seconds of impulse needs almost no fuel, but 10 lbf of thrust on 300 tonnes takes more than five years to Jupiter. Exhaust speed alone does not make a torch: power does.

tours.title: How big the radiators really are

stops.caption: The fission fragment ship throws away 700 of every 1000 MW it makes. At 1350 K the panels shed that through 1954 square metres.
stops.try: Look at the heat line in the power books.

stops.caption: Its magnets must stay at 120 K. Shedding only 0.05 MW at that temperature needs 2247 square metres, more than the 699 MW panels: radiated power goes as the fourth power of temperature.
stops.try: Halve a radiator's temperature and count how much bigger it must be.

stops.caption: The HOPE fusion ship sheds 176.5 MW at 1250 K and 33.9 MW at 800 K. The cooler load is a fifth the size and needs the bigger panel.
Seen in infrared, 1954 square metres at 1350 K glow orange-hot. Heat has to leave, and wherever it goes it can be seen.
A fusion exhaust carrying 4.8 GW is brighter still. A cloak would have to say where that light and heat go, and in SSE4 it must.
stops.try: Try marking a ship as hidden and read what the GM view says.
